answer: Neighborhood cut-set routing. Each agent picks a small set of neighbors and must route a periodic voyage through them to reach the wider graph; a cluster of cloned identities sharing few external links forms a narrow cut. The protocol caps how much traffic can cross any single cut per epoch, so clones starve unless they buy diverse connections. An attacker pays real connectivity cost per identity: unique edges to honest agents, plus the onyx fee for edge registration. A nebula of isolated clones cannot reach quorum.
